(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI) This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V.Act, 1988" for short) by the appellants-claimants being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded vide judgment and award dated 19.02.2021, passed in MVC No.17/2019 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Bailhongal (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' for short).
2. Brief facts, leading rise to the filing of this appeal, are as follows:
On 16.07.2018, at about 4.00 p.m., the deceased Prashant @ Ashok s/o Veerangouda @ Iranagouda Patil, was proceeding on his Hero-Honda motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-24/Q-6221, as a rider from Bailhongal to his native place Yaraguddi village.

At that time, one Mahindra and Mahindra Company, LMV Police vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA22/G-513, came from the opposite direction in a NC:
2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR rash and negligent manner, and dashed to the deceased.
As a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries, and during the treatment, he succumbed to the injuries.
The claimants being the legal representatives of the deceased filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act claiming compensation on account of the death of deceased person.

3. Respondent No.1-owner filed the statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contented that the driver possessed a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of accident.
It is contented that because of the fault of the rider of the motorcycle, the accident occurred and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Mahindra and Mahindra vehicle.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to dismiss the claim petition against respondent No.1-owner.
Respondent No.2 filed a memo adopting the statement of objections filed by Respondent No. 1.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR 4.
The Tribunal, based on the rival pleadings of the parties, framed the relevant issues.
5. The claimants to substantiate their case, claimant No.1 was examined as P.W.1, and marked 272 documents as Exs.P1 to P272.

Conversely, the officer of the respondents was examined as R.W.1,
and marked 5 documents as Exs.R1 to R5.
6.

The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part with costs vide judgment dated 19.02.2021, and awarded a compensation of Rs.18,17,510/- with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of the petition till the date of realization, and held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 before the Tribunal are liable to pay the entire compensation to the Smt. Meenakshi W/O Prashant Patil vs The Superintendent Of Police on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158068676/
3 claimants and respondent Nos.1 and 2 was directed to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR 7.

sentences.text: The claimants, dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, filed this Miscellaneous First Appeal.

8. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned HCGP for the respondents.
9.
Learned counsel for the claimants submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, He prays to enhance the compensation.

10. Per contra, the learned HCGP submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for any interference, at the hands of this court, and accordingly, prays to dismiss the appeal.
11.
Perused the records, and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
12. The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR 13.
There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident, and the death of the deceased in a road traffic accident.
To prove that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the claimants have produced Ex.P10-Charge Sheet.
The Tribunal was justified in recording a finding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Reg. Quantum of compensation:
14.
The claimants claimants have contended that the deceased was an agriculturist, and used to earn Rs.5,00,000/- p.a.
However, no documents are produced to prove the income.
The accident is of 2018.
The notional income has to be assessed as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Accordingly, the notional income of the deceased is taken at Rs.11,750/-
p.m.

In addition to it, 40% towards the future prospects has to be added, as per the proposition of law laid down by the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, which comes to Rs.4,700/-.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.16,450/-
(Rs.11,750 + Rs.4,700).

As the deceased was about 34 years old, the multiplier applicable to the age group of the petitioner is '16' as per the proposition of law laid down in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT) AND OTHERS V. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER reported in (2009)
6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: There are two claimants, 1/3rd is to be deducted from the income, which comes to Rs.10,967/- (Rs.16,450/- - Rs.5,483/-).

Thus, the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.21,05,664/- rounded off to Rs.21,05,600 (Rs.10,967/-x 12 x 16) under the head of loss of Smt. Meenakshi W/O Prashant Patil vs The Superintendent Of Police on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158068676/
4 dependency.

sentences.text:
The claimants are also entitled to a compensation of Rs.96,000/- (Rs.48,000/- x 2)
towards loss of consortium, and Rs.36,000/- towards the loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Thus,
the claimants are entitled for medical bills at Rs.6,94,444/-.

The Tribunal has fastened NC:
2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR the liability to the extent of 30% on the deceased.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.7,80,174/-.
15.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to a total compensation, which is as follows:
Compensation Particulars amount in (Rs.)

Loss of dependency 21,05,600 Loss of consortium 96,000 Loss of estate and funeral 36,000 expenses Medical bills 6,94,444 Total 29,32,044 Less: compensation awarded 18,17,510 by the Tribunal Total 11,14,534 Less: 30% contributory 3,34,360 negligence Enhanced compensation 7,80,174 16.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.7,80,174/-, in addition to the compensation already awarded by the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its - 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR deposit.
In view of the same, the point regarding the quantum is answered accordingly.

17. In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and the award dated 19.02.2021, passed in MVC No.17/2019 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Bailhongal, is hereby modified.

iii) The appellants-claimants are entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.7,80,174/- in addition to the compensation already awarded by the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its deposit.

iv) The respondents are directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3661 HC-KAR 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
